Every gap the review named is closed. tests.closes: The built-app journey the review asked for (a New Save choosing I Know SLATE, then no locked control and Play shown paused). The test renders SlateApp's own playing phase from the phase its Begin set. Nothing is locked: no control, panel or screen, and no lock word. The rail shows Home, Player Profile, School, Money and Papers. All five destination screens are open. Play is pressed (aria-pressed) with the clock paused, and its own onClick sends the clock live.

gapsClosed: The I Know SLATE path is untested. No test creates {tutorial:false, paused:true} and asserts no universe.tutorial, timeSpeed 'paused' and commands open.
The mapping in SlateApp.tsx:49 is untested.
The guard on a decision's command is proven only with a hand-installed guard, not the guide's.

The built app never picked I Know SLATE. The journey it was asked to show is now held as the player has it, by rendering SlateApp's playing phase after its own Begin, with the guided twin as the contrast: no lock in the shell or on any of the five destination screens, every rail destination present, Play shown paused, and Play pressed sending the clock live.

problems: Checked: the I Know SLATE path is a rendered screen, which the standard accepts. The Review radio's own onChange sets tutorial false, and Begin goes through SlateApp's own handler, giving config {tutorial:false, paused:true}. The playing phase renders the real GameShell and WorkspaceRouter over the real save: 0 locks, the rail ['Home', 'Player Profile', 'School', 'Money', 'Papers'], and all 5 routes open. Play's onClick runs the real world.set_preferences command through sim.execute, and timeSpeed goes 'live'. The guided twin is the contrast: 4 controls and 8 panels locked, the rail Home alone, each screen held shut, and Play opening the guide at 'clock' with the clock paused.

The latest skeptic called it 'heavily mocked'. useState is seeded and recorded, useKept is stubbed, and game-context is a Proxy whose unlisted members are no-ops. But the sim, its commands and the components are real, and the mutations listed (SlateApp's tutorial mapping, the GameShell rail filter, bootstrap's paused) each fail these assertions. tools/acceptance-ui.mjs still never picks I Know SLATE. The standard's 'screen rendered' covers it, so I don't count it as open.
Closed (defect 62 fixed): Play/Pause no longer carries aria-pressed (TimeControls.tsx, with a past-tense comment). The test now asserts it is absent on Play and on Pause.

The other review gaps were closed in the first round (tests/evidence-g29-ui.test.ts > c-tutorial): I Know SLATE made through SlateApp's mapping and kept across a reload, the guided life refusing Sleep, and a decision's File It held by the guide's own guard (Simulation.guardedBecause) on a game-config life.

review.claim: At tax season (1 Feb), the decision 'Your <year> Tax Return' is raised with File It, which runs tax.file. defects.where: src/engine/systems/permission.ts statusCheckAt, line 167: `if (permission > sim.now) return permission;`. The rule was tightened in both files. ONE names the possessive and adjective singulars. REMOVAL doesn't take a removal verb after a present or future auxiliary, and counts 'went' only where it ends a clause or says when or with what. A PRESENT clause with the interests as subject of a present verb fails a sentence whatever else it says. b13's NAMES and HISTORY were replaced by the same rule, and its namingIn strips money's phrases first, as evidence3's does. Five sentences the possessive singular found in the tree were read and listed true: two scene briefs and three money uses.

The second pass, from the recheck of 2026-10-15. PRESENT's plural takes any word after 'interests' but the past (-ed and the irregular forms) and the words in NOT_PRESENT (function words, nouns they compound with, 'too', and 'is', which a plural subject never takes), where it was a closed list of 46 verbs; a clause set off by commas may stand between subject and verb; the future and the modals count; and the present perfect ('have been removed') is the past's. REMOVAL's 'went' is the removal's only before a date, 'with', 'that day' or 'when', or at a clause's end, no longer before 'on', 'in the' or 'at'. ONE takes two adjectives after a possessive; after 'a' or 'the' it keeps the narrower list, since 'the last interest day' is money's. Both files carry the same rule.

review.claim: After the interests were removed (code removal and migration 94, 2026-10-10), Person.genres and Person.personality (the seven dispositions, with the traits) stay on every person, on a new life and on a save migrated from schema 93, and are still read downstream: genres by enjoyment.ts (lovedInWork/enjoyWork, mood and stress only); dispositions by personality.ts (knobs), enjoyment.ts (openness, agreeableness, extraversion via takeTheHouse), credit.ts (riskTolerance -> autopay) and attributes.ts (conscientiousness -> starting discipline, emotionalStability -> starting composure). Changes: nothing. Row cites tests/migration-94.test.ts 'drops the interests and their record, keeps the genres...' and defers 'read' to c-genres and c-disp-*.

ui.have: This is an engine-state claim. tests/defects-r8-1.test.ts:150-169 renders the Profile's 'You love:' genres, but on a new life. Nothing renders the Profile's Dispositions line (ProfileWorkspace.tsx:156), and no acceptance-ui.mjs step opens a migrated save.

gaps: The cited test, tests/migration-94.test.ts:35-46, never asserts personality or personalityTraits after migrate. The 'dispositions intact after removal' half rests on code inspection of index.ts:933-944. The fixture's default personality (newLifeConfig -> defaultPersonality, personality.ts:26-31) would also hide a 94 step that reset dispositions to defaults.
Every migration-94 test calls migrate() directly on a hand-edited universe. None opens the save through openSlot (index.ts:991-1014), the path the game uses, which also writes the migrated save back.
'Read after removal' is never shown on a migrated save. No migration-94 test runs a reader (enjoyWork, takeTheHouse, personalityOf, openCredit, derivedAbilities) on the opened 93 save.

Even on new lives, the readers are tested only by direct calls with hand-set state (traits-connected.test.ts:116-134, arrears.test.ts:53-83, personality.test.ts:378-387, ui-fixes.test.ts:42-49). No command or clock test drives a rehearsal (school.ts:3311/3555) or a night (school.ts:3548) and compares a genre lover with a non-lover, or an agreeable student with a disagreeable one.

The attributes.ts readers are weakly covered. Starting discipline from conscientiousness (attributes.ts:115) is untested. Composure from stability (attributes.test.ts:25-40) is checked only at the default stability, with the same constants as the code.
The row defers 'read' to c-genres and c-disp-*. Its own evidence (one migration test) covers only genres being kept, so the row's 'verified' overstates its own evidence.

tests.title: i-genres-dispositions-intact > PLAYER JOURNEY: a 93 save opened through openSlot keeps the personality, the trait and the genres to the figure, drops the interests, writes the save back with the 93 as its backup, and a second open changes nothing
tests.closes: The cited test asserted neither personality nor traits and used the default personality; the migration tests called migrate() directly. This one sets every axis away from creation's start (80/20/90/10/30/70/90), adds Curious, and opens through openSlot on a LocalSaveAdapter over an in-memory localStorage. It checks the slot written back at 94, the backup at 93, a second open with no steps, discipline 40 (30 + 0.5×20), composure 35.5 (25 + 0.35×30), autopay 'minimum', and the Profile's Dispositions line and 'You love: Comedy.' on the opened save

tests.title: i-genres-dispositions-intact > PLAYER JOURNEY: starts a new life’s discipline at 30 + conscientiousness ÷ 2 and its composure at 25 + 0.35 × stability, at both ends of the sliders, and the Profile says so; presence is drawn alike
tests.closes: Starting discipline from conscientiousness was untested and composure was tested only at the default stability. Now: discipline 32.5 and 77.5 at conscientiousness 5 and 95; composure 28.5 and 56.5 at stability 10 and 90; presence the same for both; the Profile shows each

gapsClosed: The cited migration test never asserted personality or personalityTraits, and its default personality would hide a reset; now a non-default personality and a trait are asserted to the figure after the open.
Every migration-94 test called migrate() directly; now the save is opened through openSlot, which writes the migrated save back (checked at 94) and keeps the 93 as the backup.

'Read after removal' was never shown on a migrated save; now enjoyWork (genres, agreeableness, openness), takeTheHouse and personalityOf are driven by the clock on opened 93 saves, and credit autopay is driven through a statement.
No command or clock test compared a genre lover with a non-lover, or an agreeable student with a disagreeable one; now both are compared on opened saves, against literal figures.
Starting discipline from conscientiousness was untested and composure was checked only at the default stability; now both are tested at both ends of the sliders.
The row's own evidence covered only the genres; now it covers the dispositions and traits as well.

problems: Every named gap is closed, with no vacuity found.

The saves are written as schema 93 (the TEST SETUP that migration-94.test.ts also uses) and opened through openSlot on a LocalSaveAdapter, the path SaveSlots.tsx:39 uses. The write-back at 94, the backup kept at 93 and a no-op second open are all checked.
After the open, the personality (80/20/90/10/30/70/90, away from creation's start on every axis), the trait 'curious' and the genres are asserted as literals. A reset to defaults would fail.

On the opened saves, the readers are driven by the clock with figures worked by hand from the rules' numbers. Drama 50 gives morale 2×(10−50)/50 = −1.6 against 0.2. The read-through gives −0.4 against 0.4. The curtain moves stress by 6×(1−c/100)×bend(1.1×1.2) − 3.2, and I checked that gain against personality.ts:73-79 and 119-129. The Tartuffe rehearsal gives the comedy lover +1.5 morale and −1.5 stress against the western lover. The autopay's $40.00 floor is paid against $270.00 for the twin.
Discipline (30 + c/2) and composure (25 + 0.35×s) are tested at both ends of the sliders, and the Profile's rendered figures are checked.

The agent's claimCorrection is right: credit.ts:1213 and attributes.ts:115 and 131 read the dispositions only when a life begins. On a migrated save their consequence is the kept value (autopay, discipline, composure) and what it drives, which the card test shows by the clock.
The run passed. Minor: composure in the curtain formula is read from the engine's state before the curtain, but as an input, not as the expected output.

claimCorrection.said: enjoyment.ts, personality.ts, credit.ts, attributes.ts
claimCorrection.now: enjoyment.ts (genres, openness and agreeableness, and extraversion through takeTheHouse at each performance's nerves) and personality.ts (emotional stability, ambition and conscientiousness, with the traits) read them at every call and night. credit.ts (risk tolerance, the card's starting autopay) and attributes.ts (conscientiousness for starting discipline, emotional stability for starting composure) read them only when a life begins, so on a save migrated from 93 what they set at creation is what's kept. Until 2026-10-13 this named all four as readers alike.

findings.what: Creation's Dispositions text says 'None of them makes you better or worse at anything', but two sliders set starting abilities read by evaluation
findings.evidence: Conscientiousness sets Discipline = 30 + 0.5*c (5 -> 32.5, 95 -> 77.5), which lifts practice (attributes.ts:263) and feeds consistency in every task. Emotional Stability sets Composure = 25 + 0.35*s. The page lists neither effect.
findings.suggestedFix: Say on the page that Conscientiousness sets your starting Discipline and Emotional Stability your starting Composure, and drop the 'None of them makes you better' sentence. The other option is to decouple the abilities from the sliders, but that is the owner's call.

findings.what: The 'receipts' knob (Chaotic 0.9, Keeps Accounts 1.3) changes nothing in play
findings.evidence: recordJobCost is the only writer of y.jobCosts and has no production caller (it appears only in tests/costs.test.ts:54 and tests/arrears.test.ts:107), so the multiplier always applies to 0. Five places still claim the effect: the creation text (CharacterCreation.tsx:655-657), the trait descriptions and costs (personality-traits.ts:177,265), KNOB_READS.receipts, the trait look, and docs/UNBITTEN.md:193-198.
findings.suggestedFix: Either wire a real job-cost source, or log this in docs/UNBITTEN.md and make the text say it in the past tense. The second option also means taking 'receipts' off Chaotic and Keeps Accounts, or marking it in the trait look as not read now.

findings.what: The Home decision's 'Apply For OPT' button quietly adds premium processing
findings.evidence: The action payload is { premium: true }, which adds premiumFee 1,780 USD (content/workrules.ts:40). Papers offers 'Apply For OPT' (standard) and 'Apply With Premium Processing' as two separate buttons (src/ui/papers/Documents.tsx:196-197). No test covers this decision.
findings.suggestedFix: Label the button 'Apply For OPT, Premium Processing', or offer both. Add a test.

findings.what: Decision buttons get around the guide's command locks
findings.evidence: Only top-level commands are guarded. world.take_decision_action opens in the 'needs' chapter (content/tutorial.ts:99) and runs tax.file, bank.reactivate or documents.apply_opt nested, even while their chapters (tutorial.ts:215,229,265) are still locked.

findings.what: Home's Papers line understates tax owed and how fast it grows
findings.evidence: Home sums the stored r.owed (as of the last accrual), while PapersWorkspace.tsx:153 uses owedOn(r, now). Home says 'growing half a percent a month', but the engine also adds 7% a year interest (taxreturn.ts:69-100). Papers states both.
findings.suggestedFix: Use owedOn(r, sim.now) and say 'interest and a late-payment penalty'.

findings.what: The Profile's genre suggestion mislabels its fallback
findings.evidence: When there is no casting play, nextGenre returns the least-known loved genre, but the sentence still says it 'is the kind your next work asks for'.
findings.suggestedFix: Make nextGenre return its reason (play or loved) and word the sentence by it.

findings.what: Traits on the Player Profile can't be opened, and dispositions appear nowhere after creation
findings.evidence: Creation says 'Once you're playing, each opens from your own page into what it moves', but the Profile prints plain names. The trait look can only be reached from the person look (looks/wellbeing.tsx:117-120).
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap each trait in <Open subject={at('trait', id)}>. Consider showing the seven dispositions as well.

findings.what: The stress dial still names 'a night on a sofa'
findings.evidence: src/engine/systems/life.ts:753-754: the friend's-sofa night went in the scope reset of 2026-10-09.

findings.what: Stale present-tense claims about the interests
findings.evidence: 'enjoyment's loved interests', and 'the reading interest's enjoyment (READ_CRAFTS...)', where READ_CRAFTS no longer exists; 'an ability, an interest, a genre'; 'An hour of practice, an interest or study'.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove them or put them in the past tense, then regenerate CAPABILITIES.md with tools/capabilities.mjs --write.

findings.what: The personality system's header says three dispositions are read by nothing
findings.evidence: systems/enjoyment.ts:82,83,121 reads openness, agreeableness and extraversion. The header also leaves out the composure and discipline readers.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the header in the past tense.

findings.what: Height and weight are dropped without a word when out of range or half filled
findings.evidence: The imperial inputs allow up to 7 ft 11 in (241 cm), and settle() is skipped above 230 cm or when only one of the two is given. The body is then drawn from the birthplace and no message says so. No test passes heightCm through createUniverse.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a validate() message on Starting Point, and a creation test.

findings.what: Live decisions carry refTypes that have no look, while a comment says only older saves carry refTypes
findings.evidence: 'return', 'unclaimed-notice' and 'us-status' are written today. lookExists guards against a dead link, but the decision look offers no way onto the account or the return.
findings.suggestedFix: Map these refTypes to account and document subjects, and fix the comment.

findings.what: The US status decision stays open after OPT is applied for from Papers, and its comment is stale
findings.evidence: apply_opt does not resolve the 'us-status' decision. Its detail ('OPT can still be applied for') and its button stay until dueAt, and pressing the button is refused ('You've applied for OPT already'). The comment 'with the way home' is stale; the move home went on 2026-10-09.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the us-status decision inside documents.apply_opt.

findings.what: A broken doc-comment fragment in Home
findings.evidence: '/** Where the life began:    </>  );  }' merges into the next JSDoc. It compiles, but it is a leftover of a bad edit.

findings.what: No test covers the risk tolerance card reader
findings.evidence: No test sets riskTolerance > 65 and expects autopay to be 'minimum'.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a creation test at 90 and at 50.
